requirements.title: Reproducible identity
requirements.acceptance: Every result names commit plus dirty-source hashes, active engine, profile, seed, units, engine/OS/device, render and input settings. A result for an experimental or native engine cannot certify gameplay.
requirements.verification: Attach a manifest and demonstrate which stepper GameController instantiates in the tested artifact.
requirements.counterexample: Green native tests while the exported app runs different GDScript.

requirements.title: Requirement evidence ledger
requirements.acceptance: Every required ID has PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN, BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE in the execution ledger. Attempted claims link raw artifacts; blocked rows name the missing prerequisite. Passing requires expected/actual results, oracle identity and uncertainty. Catalog UNVERIFIED is not a passed execution status.
requirements.verification: Check the complete catalog against the final ledger; no missing IDs.
requirements.counterexample: A report contains only a total assertion count.

requirements.title: Independent oracle
requirements.acceptance: Each numerical claim uses an independently derived analytic result, sourced experiment or separately validated implementation with documented assumptions. Differential agreement alone is insufficient.
requirements.verification: For each family name a plausible wrong implementation and show a discriminator.
requirements.counterexample: Two engines share the same erroneous formula and agree.

requirements.title: Reference provenance
requirements.acceptance: Competitor claims name build/platform/mode/cue/table and timecodes; unknown fields remain unknown. Edited GIF timing supplies no latency, friction or speed coefficient.
requirements.verification: Audit each statement against the actual clip/interaction and source ledger.
requirements.counterexample: Treat a HUD timer reset as continuous physical time.

requirements.title: Executable evidence integrity
requirements.acceptance: Acceptance checks exit nonzero for failed assertions, script/parse errors, capture failure and invalid output. Harness timeout is a failure to establish the target.
requirements.verification: Inject one bad result, broken dependency and unwritable output path.
requirements.counterexample: Godot exits zero after a script parse error.

requirements.title: Threshold integrity
requirements.acceptance: Use this revision unchanged for a run. A revision records old/new value, reason, source, impact, reviewer and retained failing evidence before a new acceptance run.
requirements.verification: Review contract revisions and compare old/new fixtures.
requirements.counterexample: Delete an outlier seed or increase tolerance until green.

requirements.title: Worst-case reporting
requirements.acceptance: Publish each family and profile separately, sample counts, worst case, median and p95 where defined; distributions never replace exact safety invariants.
requirements.verification: Recompute summaries from raw records.
requirements.counterexample: Average easy rolls with failing grazing contacts.

requirements.title: No hidden assistance
requirements.acceptance: Any aim/shot assistance is an explicit selectable mode and recorded in fixtures; deterministic physical results do not change to favor a pot.
requirements.verification: Replay identical physical inputs with guide/UI toggles and compare states.
requirements.counterexample: Secretly steer the cue ball to the drawn guide.

requirements.title: Declared equipment profile
requirements.acceptance: Ship a versioned reference profile. Existing 9-foot profile uses 2.54 by 1.27 m, ball diameter 57.15 mm and mass 0.168 kg; declare all tolerances and source pages. Geometry values are profile choices inside a sourced range, not universal tables.
requirements.verification: Independently measure generated coordinates and profile manifest; consult WPA sections 5,7,9,16.
requirements.counterexample: Correct settings labels with meshes scaled in centimeters.

requirements.title: Shared contact surfaces
requirements.acceptance: Render, collision, support, placement and guide queries consume the same immutable mouth/jaw/slate/nose description. Maximum visible/contact boundary discrepancy <=0.25 mm in world space in both cameras and all LODs.
requirements.verification: Overlay sampled collision curves on unlit mesh sections and measure signed distances.
requirements.counterexample: A decorative pocket disk conceals an uncut cloth plane.

requirements.title: Complete pocket construction
requirements.acceptance: Each of six pockets has explicit mouth, finite facing/jaw, nose cross-section, shelf, fall edge, lining and capture volume. Corner/side distinctions survive mirroring.
requirements.verification: Inspect dimensions, section diagrams, simple polygons, contact normals and open volumes for all IDs.
requirements.counterexample: Six differently placed copies of one radius trigger.

requirements.title: Published range interpretation
requirements.acceptance: Reference profile mouth widths, shelf depths, cut angles and nose height trace to WPA or a measured table. Source-range compliance is not calibration. Preserve diagrammed angle conventions.
requirements.verification: Verify endpoint distances, angle calculations and shelf measured along pocket axis from mouth center.
requirements.counterexample: Use an interior angle as the jaw deflection, or apply corner shelf depth to side pockets.

requirements.title: Solid sphere contact datum
requirements.acceptance: Ball center height R is tangent to slate y=0. Mesh radius and physical radius differ by <=0.01 mm; no shader-dependent enlargement to improve identity.
requirements.verification: Measure world transforms and mesh bounds at supported, airborne and falling states.
requirements.counterexample: Raise cloth 2 mm through the ball to hide a shadow.

requirements.title: Normals and seams
requirements.acceptance: Contact normals are unit within 1e-6; every contacting seam has an unambiguous outward side. Rendered top normals face out, and adjacent intended contact surfaces have no gap >0.05 mm.
requirements.verification: Sample joins, segment endpoints and cross-sections; render front/back debug colors.
requirements.counterexample: A reversed triangle passes scalar dimension tests but disappears from above.

requirements.title: Finite endpoints
requirements.acceptance: Nose, jaw endpoint and corner contacts use the actual finite shape, including declared rounding. No zero-width converging throat or invisible infinite plane.
requirements.verification: Sweep approaches around both endpoints at 0.1 mm spacing, refine contact boundary to 0.01 mm.
requirements.counterexample: A ball reflects from an extrapolated rail inside a pocket.

requirements.title: Support boundary consistency
requirements.acceptance: Support/volume queries agree with mesh geometry within 0.01 mm for sampled boundary points; test both sides at 1,10,50,100 micrometers and exact edge.
requirements.verification: Independent point/triangle and edge-distance tests over the same exported geometry.
requirements.counterexample: One inclusive-boundary epsilon quietly creates a large capture strip.

requirements.title: Profile changes and cache safety
requirements.acceptance: Every parameter used by a derived surface invalidates its cache. Rendering, guides and audio cannot mutate geometry/profile state.
requirements.verification: Vary each parameter individually; hash shared data before/after 10000 queries and scene rebuilds.
requirements.counterexample: A cached jaw updates while support polygons remain old.

requirements.title: Placement validity
requirements.acceptance: Cue placement requires full supported sphere clearance from other balls, physical rails/jaws and unsupported openings, within 0.05 mm query tolerance. Preview and confirmation agree.
requirements.verification: Boundary corpus plus confirm at every displayed valid/invalid transition.
requirements.counterexample: Center point is on cloth but half the ball intersects a cushion.

requirements.title: Cue obstruction and clearance
requirements.acceptance: Ordinary stance includes shaft/tip/ferrule clearance; no cue penetration >0.25 mm into rail or balls during aim/stroke. A physically unavailable stroke is visibly blocked or uses a validated elevated stance.
requirements.verification: Sweep cue-ball rail distance, direction and tip offsets; inspect full cue swept volume.
requirements.counterexample: A perfect impulse is generated by a cue drawn through a rail.

requirements.title: Round-trip geometry
requirements.acceptance: Serialization and profile reload preserve dimensions to <=1 micrometer and preserve pocket IDs, handedness and normals exactly in meaning.
requirements.verification: Export/reload two profiles and repeat support/contact queries.
requirements.counterexample: x/z or millimeter/meter swap survives a screenshot test.

requirements.title: Intent retention
requirements.acceptance: Unpressed motion, GUI use and GUI-origin drags change retained physical aim by <=1e-7 rad; deliberate acquisition, release and cancellation are explicit.
requirements.verification: Real Viewport routing and native mouse/trackpad sequences through HUD, outside release and focus changes.
requirements.counterexample: Calling only the controller input method misses GUI capture.

requirements.title: Reachable fine angle
requirements.acceptance: Provide a precise input path with independently selectable increments <=0.005 degrees and reversible repeatability <=0.002 degrees; coarse input remains fast.
requirements.verification: 100 positive/negative increments at several headings, zooms, DPI and windows; measure physical direction.
requirements.counterexample: Readout changes more finely than the actual shot direction.

requirements.title: Pointer mapping
requirements.acceptance: Picking/reprojection error <=0.5 framebuffer pixel for valid table points; stationary pointer drift <=0.25 pixel after transforms settle. Distinguish framebuffer pixels from OS logical points.
requirements.verification: Grid and near-rail targets in both cameras, aspect/Retina changes and window moves.
requirements.counterexample: An overhead-only picking test masks a lounge-camera offset.

requirements.title: Fine intent task
requirements.acceptance: In a pilot, trained users can repeatedly acquire a long straight shot within 0.05 degrees; median acquisition <=3 s after familiarization, accidental aim loss <=1% of attempts. Final panel also applies.
requirements.verification: At least 8 pilot users, 20 randomized acquisitions each; record heading error/time and mistakes, stratified by experience.
requirements.counterexample: Machine has tiny steps but people overshoot or cannot discover them.

requirements.title: Guide promise
requirements.acceptance: Default guide states its exact prediction scope. First-contact geometry and launch direction match the active solver within 0.25 mm /0.02 degrees on the named static corpus; later paths are shown only when separately validated.
requirements.verification: Overlay guide and simulated first-contact point over speed/spin/cut sweeps.
requirements.counterexample: Draw a confident outgoing ray that omits throw.

requirements.title: Uncertainty and identity
requirements.acceptance: A guide that cannot meet its bound is shortened, visibly qualified or omitted; real balls versus guide ghosts are correctly identified >=95% in blinded gameplay-scale trials.
requirements.verification: Dark/striped balls, clusters, tangencies, occlusion and guide-off comparisons.
requirements.counterexample: A filled ghost is mistaken for a target ball.

requirements.title: No hidden aim snap
requirements.acceptance: No discontinuous angular snap >0.005 degrees during continuous fine input except a separately enabled, indicated snapping mode.
requirements.verification: Dense pointer sweep across targets, rails, cue center and GUI boundaries.
requirements.counterexample: Auto-pot snapping is hidden as precision assistance.

requirements.title: Focus and modality
requirements.acceptance: Menu, focus loss, resize/DPI changes, camera transition, placement, undo and stroke commitment terminate incompatible gestures. Re-entry never resumes from a stale held flag.
requirements.verification: Transition graph tests with pressed/missed-release events and native capture.
requirements.counterexample: Release was consumed by a menu; later motion unexpectedly aims.

requirements.title: Keyboard access
requirements.acceptance: Every essential practice operation is keyboard reachable with visible focus; aim and spin contexts are unambiguous and cancel/reset are consistent after GUI actions.
requirements.verification: Complete a shot, spin selection, undo, scratch placement and pause with keyboard alone.
requirements.counterexample: A focused slider silently steals global fine-aim keys.

requirements.title: Response latency
requirements.acceptance: On declared 60 Hz baseline hardware, native input to first correct visible aim response: p95<=25 ms, p99<=40 ms, no unexplained >100 ms stall in 1000 adjustments.
requirements.verification: Timestamp input and displayed output using calibrated capture; measure mouse and trackpad separately.
requirements.counterexample: Internal handler timestamps exclude queued frames and display delay.

requirements.title: Physical meaning
requirements.acceptance: Specify input displacement -> authored power -> cue speed -> impulse -> ball speed/spin. A percentage is not force in newtons. If force is exposed, its integral and contact-time model must reproduce impulse.
requirements.verification: Trace units and each mapping; independently audit energy/work.
requirements.counterexample: Equal slider percentages are asserted to mean equal kinetic energy.

requirements.title: Delicate minimum
requirements.acceptance: Zero does not animate, count, sound or fire. Minimum useful nonzero selectable center shot travels 10–30 mm on the frozen reference cloth. Every reachable nonzero setting above that minimum yields measurable motion.
requirements.verification: Dense low-end UI sweep using actual controller-to-settle behavior, not a copied formula.
requirements.counterexample: Increase rolling friction until a coarse minimum shot looks short.

requirements.title: Target distance resolution
requirements.acceptance: Nearest machine-selectable unobstructed center strokes can land at 50,100,200,500,1000 mm within max(2 mm,1% of target). Adjacent settings in the 20–200 mm travel range differ by <=2 mm.
requirements.verification: Sweep actual reachable input states; report nearest attainable endpoints and unsatisfied gaps.
requirements.counterexample: Fine display decimals conceal coarse actual input quantization.

requirements.title: Full range and monotonicity
requirements.acceptance: Preserve the declared full stroke range; current reference maximum cue speed is 8 m/s until a sourced profile revision. At least 101 settings plus every low-end UI quantum have strictly increasing launch speed and smooth travel response outside physical outcome boundaries.
requirements.verification: No-rail power/travel plot; compare old/new maximum and curve derivatives.
requirements.counterexample: Improve soft shots by removing the break range or hide a dead band.

requirements.title: Repeatable selection
requirements.acceptance: Identical committed input/profile produces identical speed/spin on one build. In pilot landing tasks, median absolute error <=5 mm for 50–200 mm targets and <=2% for 500–1000 mm, after practice.
requirements.verification: Separate machine reachability from human selection, at least 20 repetitions per target/user.
requirements.counterexample: Tuned bot values pass while the mouse cannot select them.

requirements.title: Valid and finite input
requirements.acceptance: Zero, negative, nonfinite, out-of-range, canceled and repeated inputs have explicit behavior; each physical commitment fires once. Readout corresponds to committed resolution.
requirements.verification: Real controller and UI malformed/boundary requests; hold and release through focus changes.
requirements.counterexample: A zero setting still adds a stroke, or two callbacks fire.

requirements.title: Energy and impulse
requirements.acceptance: For a legal resting-ball strike, ball kinetic-energy gain (translation+rotation) <=0.5*m_cue*v_cue² plus declared external work and max(1e-9 J,1e-6*input energy). A closed cue+ball model also accounts for outgoing cue/recoil and losses. Unsupported moving-ball strikes are explicitly rejected or separately validated.
requirements.verification: Independent effective-mass/energy cases and a speed/offset/elevation grid.
requirements.counterexample: Linear speed is bounded but spin adds unaccounted energy.

requirements.title: Contact point mapping
requirements.acceptance: Input axes, rendered tip and physical contact arm agree within 0.1 mm. Top/bottom/left/right/diagonal signs are verified in both cameras.
requirements.verification: Inspect world contact coordinates and resulting spin; perturb each sign independently.
requirements.counterexample: UI says draw while the physical contact is above center.

requirements.title: Offset behavior
requirements.acceptance: Launch speed/spin, squirt and miscue boundary agree with a sourced model/measurement within calibration bounds; include combined offsets and near-limit cases.
requirements.verification: Fit/hold out families with r/R=0,.1,.25,.45,.49,.50 and points just outside supported domain.
requirements.counterexample: Only cardinal-axis spin cases work.

requirements.title: Delivered speed coherence
requirements.acceptance: Continuous visual tip velocity at contact agrees with the commanded physical cue speed within 10%; derive motion travel/duration consistently. Displayed frame samples match the integrated trajectory rather than a separately timed fake hit.
requirements.verification: Analytic motion-curve audit and high-frame-rate rendered capture for soft/medium/hard delivery.
requirements.counterexample: A fixed 75 ms tween depicts 2 m/s while physics delivers 6 m/s.

requirements.title: Contact synchronization
requirements.acceptance: One committed stroke emits exactly one physical impulse at tip contact; world-space contact error <=0.1 mm and first visible ball motion is within one rendered 60 Hz frame. Selected inputs are frozen until impact.
requirements.verification: Capture rendered contact plus impulse state; mutate pending UI values and compare delivered shot.
requirements.counterexample: A timer fires independently of cue animation.

requirements.title: Clearance and ordinary elevation
requirements.acceptance: Final required coverage includes physically valid ordinary elevated stances from0 to10 degrees and usable rail-adjacent shots with cue clearance. Geometrically impossible strokes are visibly blocked. Reject unsupported candidates during development, but declaring all everyday elevated strokes unavailable does not pass this gate.
requirements.verification: Obstacle-distance/elevation/offset matrix with swept cue volume and ball launch.
requirements.counterexample: The interface hides a common clearance limitation until the shot behaves wrong.

requirements.title: Squirt and swerve distinction
requirements.acceptance: Initial deflection and subsequent cloth-driven curvature are separately represented and calibrated where ordinary elevation is supported; signs and speed/elevation dependence are tested.
requirements.verification: Matched center/left/right and mirrored elevated families with tracked trajectories.
requirements.counterexample: Add permanent sideways acceleration for all side spin.

requirements.title: Commit/cancel motion
requirements.acceptance: Input acknowledgement appears within one frame; deliberate stroke timing is explicit. Cancel, menu/reset/focus loss before contact produce no impulse, sound or score; after contact never undo an already delivered impulse implicitly.
requirements.verification: Interrupt at 0/25/50/90/99/100% of authored delivery timeline.
requirements.counterexample: A canceled tween later shoots after resume.

requirements.title: Analytic rolling
requirements.acceptance: For a calibrated constant-resistance ideal fixture, speed, stopping time and distance error <=0.1% relative with appropriate near-zero absolute tolerances. Test several speeds and durations.
requirements.verification: Use v(t)=max(v0-mu_r*g*t,0), distance v 0²/(2*mu_r*g) and stopping time v0/(mu_r*g).
requirements.counterexample: Endpoint is correct only because sleep truncates a wrong deceleration.

requirements.title: Slide-to-roll transition
requirements.acceptance: Ideal homogeneous-sphere sliding transition time, displacement and speed agree within 0.1%; residual contact slip <=1e-4 m/s at transition, with no velocity/spin discontinuity.
requirements.verification: Use independent slip/torque equations and full transition traces, including reversed slip.
requirements.counterexample: A threshold toggles between regimes and adds energy.

requirements.title: Pure rolling kinematics
requirements.acceptance: Contact slip stays <=1e-4 m/s and integrated orientation error <=0.25 degrees over 1 m for the ideal no-slip fixture.
requirements.verification: Marked sphere translation/rotation oracle on axis and diagonal paths.
requirements.counterexample: A ball center moves correctly while its texture skates.

requirements.title: Follow/draw/stun repertoire
requirements.acceptance: Measured center, follow, draw and stun shots meet the calibrated trajectory/endpoint bounds independently across distance and speed, including draw reversal and combined english.
requirements.verification: At least 5 initial speeds,3 cue-object distances, signed top offsets and held-out combinations.
requirements.counterexample: One tuned draw shot passes; longer draw becomes unintended follow.

requirements.title: Spin-in-place and decay
requirements.acceptance: Pure sidespin decays monotonically under the declared model and stays within measured angular-decay bounds; no unsupported lateral drift >0.1 mm on the ideal level/isotropic fixture.
requirements.verification: Zero-translation spin tests both signs, then compare sourced/measured traces.
requirements.counterexample: Spin friction accidentally accelerates the ball sideways.

requirements.title: Last millimeters and sleep
requirements.acceptance: Sleep removes <=0.05 mm of remaining ideal rolling travel and causes no position/orientation snap. Ready state waits for relevant motion; no fixed shot timeout forces rest.
requirements.verification: Derive tail bound from v²/(2*mu_r*g), inspect slow motion at 30/60/120 Hz and prolonged spin.
requirements.counterexample: A velocity-only .012 m/s cutoff would discard about 0.61 mm on this cloth; test the actual compound sleep condition rather than assuming that omission.

requirements.title: Cloth profile variation
requirements.acceptance: Each cloth preset has sourced/calibrated parameter ranges and held-out behavior; directional drift/nap/random skid is an explicit separate model when supported.
requirements.verification: Sensitivity plots, profile swaps and reproducibility checks with variation disabled.
requirements.counterexample: Random drift is introduced to hide systematic model error.

requirements.title: Elastic isolated conservation
requirements.acceptance: Frictionless equal-mass isolated impacts preserve total momentum and kinetic energy within1e-6 relative or1e-9 in corresponding SI absolute units; outgoing vectors meet the analytic solution.
requirements.verification: Head-on/cut/moving-target and 3 D-height fixtures with independent vector solution.
requirements.counterexample: Correct departure angle but incorrect transferred speed.

requirements.title: Dissipative accounting
requirements.acceptance: At isolated contacts with no external work, translational+rotational energy cannot increase by >1e-6 relative or1e-9 J. Record normal/tangent impulses and losses.
requirements.verification: Before/after same-position contact ledger and pure spin-transfer cases.
requirements.counterexample: Friction removes translation but creates too much rotation.

requirements.title: Impact timing
requirements.acceptance: Isolated sphere contact-time error <=10 microseconds +2 micrometers/normal closing speed for well-conditioned contacts. Grazing cases use closest-approach/boundary error <=2 micrometers, not division by a near-zero speed.
requirements.verification: Analytic quadratic roots, time-phase sweep, exact-touch and near-gap cases.
requirements.counterexample: Use the correct normal after integrating an entire overlap interval.

requirements.title: Thin cuts and tangencies
requirements.acceptance: Outside the declared contact uncertainty band (<=2 micrometers), legal thin hits and true clearances are classified correctly. Inside it, report tolerance-limited classification. Ideal outgoing direction error <=0.02 degrees when speed>=0.05 m/s; slower outputs use vector error bounds.
requirements.verification: Cut angles 0–89.9 degrees, refine around tangent at micrometer offsets and mirror both sides.
requirements.counterexample: A broad epsilon causes ghost contacts or suppresses valid grazes.

requirements.title: Throw and spin transfer
requirements.acceptance: Cut-induced/spin-induced throw, gearing, follow/draw interaction and spin transfer meet sourced/measured bounds; absence/sign-change locations are tested.
requirements.verification: Independent sourced curves within their domain and held-out speed/cut/spin grids.
requirements.counterexample: Constant tangential correction matches one cut but reverses gearing behavior.

requirements.title: Frozen and simultaneous contacts
requirements.acceptance: Touching pairs,3/4-ball chains, double kisses and tight racks have finite, converged observable outcomes under a declared contact law. Individual simultaneous-contact impulses are checked only against an appropriate solver/contact-law oracle, not an assumed universal unique decomposition.
requirements.verification: Symmetric and asymmetric multi-contact corpus with increasing solver quality.
requirements.counterexample: A single pair sweep hides cluster order dependence.

requirements.title: Penetration budget
requirements.acceptance: Immediately before contact resolution, isolated penetration <=0.01 mm and dense-cluster transient penetration<=0.2 mm. Record post-resolution residual separately; every settled overlap<=0.05 mm. Bounds include all declared slop. Report worst pair/time, not an average.
requirements.verification: Measure every substep across the stress corpus; retain offending states.
requirements.counterexample: Position correction leaves a visibly compressed frozen rack.

requirements.title: Contact identity and order
requirements.acceptance: Events distinguish true physical contacts from numerical solver iterations. First contact, repeated distinct impacts and separations have stable chronological identity with declared simultaneous-event tie semantics.
requirements.verification: Inspect raw event times/pairs and separated/repeated-contact fixtures.
requirements.counterexample: One collision produces six sounds or suppresses a later double kiss.

requirements.title: Geometry-aware contact
requirements.acceptance: Contact location/normal follows nose height, finite shape and sphere height; no rectangular fallback changes rail position at pockets. Ideal geometric contact error <=0.01 mm.
requirements.verification: Height/incidence/endpoint sweeps with mesh-section oracle.
requirements.counterexample: A ball clears the visible nose but collides with a full-height wall.

requirements.title: Speed-angle-spin response
requirements.acceptance: For measured supported rail families, outgoing angle median error<=0.15 degrees and p95<=0.5 degrees; speed-ratio median error<=2% and p95<=5%; spin must meet CAL bounds.
requirements.verification: Repeat at several speeds, incidence angles and both english signs; hold out entire families.
requirements.counterexample: Tune one restitution scalar to one perpendicular bounce.

requirements.title: Coupled support reaction
requirements.acceptance: Rail/slate forces and friction form one consistent contact model. Downward impulses are reacted/accounted for rather than silently discarded; small hops and landing are finite and calibrated where present.
requirements.verification: Log 3 D impulse/work, vertical state, normal loads and post-impact slip through contact.
requirements.counterexample: Reset vertical velocity next tick and call that a validated slate reaction.

requirements.title: Running/reverse english
requirements.acceptance: Mirror-related shots mirror, running/reverse responses vary continuously away from physical regime boundaries, and tangent/normal components have the sourced signs.
requirements.verification: Incidence 5/15/30/45/60/75/85 degrees and signed spin ratios.
requirements.counterexample: A visually plausible bank has reversed spin or a sign error on one rail.

requirements.title: Published model domain
requirements.acceptance: Every paper-derived rail model records its ball/cushion/material assumptions and speed domain. Mathavan 2010 rigid-cushion results are a limited oracle, not a universal 8 m/s preset.
requirements.verification: Read source equations/validation limits; test below/near/above the stated limit using different evidence above it.
requirements.counterexample: Apply a snooker rigid-cushion coefficient to every fast pool break.

requirements.title: Near-parallel and repeated rails
requirements.acceptance: Grazing/rail-hugging shots neither stick nor gain energy; multiple cushion paths preserve correct event counts and calibrated losses.
requirements.verification: Long near-parallel rolls, spin reversals and 2/3-rail position drills.
requirements.counterexample: A ball jitters forever along a straight rail or tunnels past a jaw.

requirements.title: Facing and main cushion distinction
requirements.acceptance: Jaw/facing and cushion responses use declared material geometry and calibration; equality is allowed only with evidence, not by convenience.
requirements.verification: Compare same incoming state on rubber nose, facing and recessed liner.
requirements.counterexample: Every rail-like contact uses the same restitution despite visibly different outcomes.

requirements.title: Support before gravity
requirements.acceptance: Supported resting balls remain supported indefinitely. Unsupported balls descend under gravity/contact forces with no injected capture velocity or attracting force.
requirements.verification: All six shelf/edge positions, exact boundary and epsilon pairs,100 s stationary holds.
requirements.counterexample: Crossing a rectangular trigger gives an immediate downward kick.

requirements.title: Partial descent remains physical
requirements.acceptance: Balls near a shelf/facing/other ball remain collidable until geometrically separated below the playable volume. Legitimate re-entry occurs before irreversible capture.
requirements.verification: Two-ball pocket collisions, jaw-first in/out paths, hanging balls and support recovery.
requirements.counterexample: FALLING state disables collisions and guarantees a pot.

requirements.title: No supported-bed scoring
requirements.acceptance: Zero pots caused by penetrating solid slate or bypassing the real opening. The first irreversible capture must follow a valid 3 D free-volume entry path. A2 D bed projection alone is not an oracle; a legitimately captured downstream return may pass beneath the bed.
requirements.verification: Replay fast center/jaw and retained 8 m/s counterexamples using sphere/solid membership, entry history, contact and scoring events on all pockets.
requirements.counterexample: A liner rebound travels under the table and is counted as pocketed.

requirements.title: Capture lifecycle
requirements.acceptance: Exactly one capture event occurs after the ball is irreversibly inside the matching pocket volume below the slate. Off-table and captured outcomes are distinct and conserved in the ball inventory.
requirements.verification: Full per-ball lifecycle ledger through high-speed entry, rejection, scratch and return presentation.
requirements.counterexample: Score at mouth entry; later reject without undoing an already granted pot.

requirements.title: Acceptance boundary fidelity
requirements.acceptance: Against a measured pocket, stable pot/reject classifications agree >=95% outside the measured transition band. Predicted transition location differs <=2 mm at the mouth or <=0.25 degrees in approach angle, whichever scan is used.
requirements.verification: Rasterize outcome maps, repeat boundary shots and estimate natural variability; report confusion by pocket/speed.
requirements.counterexample: Tune a generous radius until most clean-center pots succeed.

requirements.title: Speed and spin dependence
requirements.acceptance: Slow center drop, rail-hugging entry, high-speed rejection, jaw-rattle, double-jaw and signed-spin families are independently validated for corners and sides.
requirements.verification: Use F-POCKET scan axes and repeat both mirror signs.
requirements.counterexample: One easy pocket entry is treated as proof of all pocket behavior.

requirements.title: Shelf and edge behavior
requirements.acceptance: A ball can rest/hang, roll off and return according to actual geometry; the edge reaction has bounded energy/projection error and passes numerical refinement.
requirements.verification: Slow near-threshold shots with energy/potential ledger and refined geometry/time step.
requirements.counterexample: A position correction creates an unexplained jump or sticky equilibrium.

requirements.title: Rendered descent
requirements.acceptance: Visible ball-node/mesh world transforms agree with physics within 0.25 mm through entry/descent; assess that subpixel bound in world space. Image-space evidence separately establishes continuous occlusion/rotation/shadow/disappearance and no visible suspension/pop-through.
requirements.verification: Frame-by-frame overhead/lounge shots, including slow edge descent and high-speed entry.
requirements.counterexample: A depth cutoff hides a floating ball before it reaches the return path.

requirements.title: Pot identity feedback
requirements.acceptance: Each pot has a clear retained identity/progress update within 100 ms of capture, never before it; scratch is visually distinct. Cosmetic return/celebration cannot change the physical outcome.
requirements.verification: Capture setup→entry→capture→feedback→ready; include simultaneous pots and undo.
requirements.counterexample: A count changes but the player cannot tell which ball disappeared.

requirements.title: Stable terminal storage
requirements.acceptance: Every ball is active, captured or off-table exactly once. Hidden pocket storage is bounded, finite and deterministic; visible stacks/returns are collision-consistent or an explicit cosmetic presentation.
requirements.verification: Repeated multi-pot clears, six-ball pocket load and reset/restore cycles.
requirements.counterexample: Hidden pocket bodies keep simulating unbounded positions or leak into a later rack.

requirements.title: Quiet final convergence
requirements.acceptance: On identical smooth/isolated initial states at matched horizons, two successive high-quality refinements converge to <=0.10 mm endpoint difference and <=0.02 degrees departure difference. Demonstrate at least three refinement levels.
requirements.verification: 240/480/960/1920 Hz or equivalent event tolerances, then continue until plateau; distinguish transient versus final.
requirements.counterexample: Only the finest level is tested, or horizon differs by one tick.

requirements.title: Production error budget
requirements.acceptance: Production settings differ from the independently validated high-quality result by <=0.25 mm and <=0.05 degrees on every quiet family; physical calibration error is reported separately.
requirements.verification: Compare actual shipped solver/profile to reference at matched times and first-contact events.
requirements.counterexample: An experimental engine meets the bound while the app uses another path.

requirements.title: Scale-aware tolerances
requirements.acceptance: Each epsilon has units, magnitude rationale and a float-precision budget. Numerical contact tolerance <=2 micrometers on the supported table domain; separating pairs beyond it do not collide.
requirements.verification: ULP/gap/tangent probes at center and far coordinates; exact-touch approaching and separating cases.
requirements.counterexample: A0.1 nm nudge rounds away in Vector2 float32 or one epsilon is reused for squared distance and speed.

requirements.title: No tunneling
requirements.acceptance: No missed ball/rail/jaw/slate crossing in the declared maximum-speed domain including full-phase and grazing sweeps. Failure is explicit outside that domain.
requirements.verification: Swept analytic or independently oversampled collision oracle, translated and time-shifted fixtures.
requirements.counterexample: A speed cap silently clips a legal break to conceal missed contacts.

requirements.title: Conservation ledger
requirements.acceptance: Elastic isolated pair momentum/energy and dissipative contact budgets satisfy BAL gates. Gravity potential, cue work, projection work and removed/captured states are separately accounted for in system-level energy.
requirements.verification: Record per-step before/after total energy and nonphysical residuals.
requirements.counterexample: Kinetic energy grows during a fall and is falsely called numerical gain, or projection work is ignored.

requirements.title: Mirror and rotation covariance
requirements.acceptance: For valid symmetries, endpoint differences <=0.01 mm, speed differences<=1e-5 m/s and spin differences<=1e-4 rad/s. Angular velocity uses axial-vector transform det(M)*M; geometry and cue inputs transform too.
requirements.verification: Both table reflection axes and 180-degree rotation; compare transformed events by semantic identity.
requirements.counterexample: Mirror angular velocity as an ordinary position vector.

requirements.title: Storage-order sensitivity
requirements.acceptance: Permutation of ball storage changes quiet outcomes by <=0.10 mm/0.02 degrees; simultaneous clusters meet a declared converged solution budget and no classification bias by ID.
requirements.verification: At least 24 permutations for representative clusters and reversed rack traversal; stable IDs stay attached.
requirements.counterexample: Renumbering balls changes a straight frozen-chain outcome.

requirements.title: Frame-chunk independence
requirements.acceptance: On one binary/profile and equal fixed-tick schedules,30/60/120/144 Hz render chunks and injected stalls yield identical canonical physical states/events; compare at equal simulation ticks, not arbitrary wall times.
requirements.verification: Chunk/replay fixtures and full trace hashes through undo/save/restore.
requirements.counterexample: Dropped accumulated time makes the game run slower during a stall.

requirements.title: Budget exhaustion visibility
requirements.acceptance: All event/iteration/catch-up limits emit auditable diagnostics; zero unreported exhaustion. Shipped stress corpus has zero accuracy-changing fallbacks. Overload policy preserves explicit simulation semantics.
requirements.verification: Frozen chains and adversarial contacts exceed prototype limits; verify failure/reporting and bound sensitivity.
requirements.counterexample: A16-event cap silently reverts to a less accurate solver.

requirements.title: Stress ladder
requirements.acceptance: Pass 1000 development then 10000 release seeded legal breaks plus difficult clusters. No nonfinite/lost balls, no safety-invariant failures; settled overlap<=0.05 mm. Retain every failing seed.
requirements.verification: Record sampled transient energy/contact diagnostics and simulate to actual rest, not a 1000-tick cutoff.
requirements.counterexample: Twenty short breaks are labelled a completed release stress test.

requirements.title: Long-session stability
requirements.acceptance: Ten-thousand reset/shot/undo/load cycles preserve state invariants and deterministic replay; invalid inputs return explicit failure without state mutation.
requirements.verification: Lifecycle stress with resource and memory accounting, including interrupted strokes.
requirements.counterexample: A capture-event suppression map survives into a new rack.

requirements.title: Cross-platform scope
requirements.acceptance: Every advertised platform/architecture passes shared numerical fixtures. Bitwise cross-platform equality is claimed only if demonstrated; otherwise publish strict bounded divergence and classification policy.
requirements.verification: Same fixture hashes on each supported build, compiler/precision metadata recorded.
requirements.counterexample: One Mac result is presented as Android or universal determinism.

requirements.title: Measured reference set
requirements.acceptance: Acquire identifiable table/ball/cue shots with full initial state estimates, scale/time calibration, repeated trials and 95% measurement uncertainty. Preserve raw footage and tracking data.
requirements.verification: Acquisition protocol and independently retracked subset; source/license/access recorded.
requirements.counterexample: Fit an unknown YouTube highlight with hidden cue stats.

requirements.title: Instrument adequacy
requirements.acceptance: For fine measured-trajectory gates, expanded uncertainty U95<=1 mm position,0.1 degrees direction, 1% speed and 1 ms time. Spin U95<=5% when |omega|>=1 rad/s and<=0.02 rad/s below it. Use suitable instrument/oracle per gate; inadequate uncertainty leaves the claim unestablished.
requirements.verification: Calibration target, clock/rolling-shutter checks, occlusion error and uncertainty propagation.
requirements.counterexample: Set test tolerance equal to an imprecise tracker error without labeling it.

requirements.title: Held-out trajectories
requirements.acceptance: Per named smooth/isolated family: trajectory RMS error<=2 mm,95 th point error<=5 mm; endpoint median<=3 mm and p95<=8 mm on the measured reference profile. Report time-aligned and path-shape errors separately.
requirements.verification: Fit only training families; compare held-out speeds/angles/offset combinations and repeated natural variability.
requirements.counterexample: Optimize endpoint while trajectory timing or intermediate path remains wrong.

requirements.title: Velocity, spin and direction
requirements.acceptance: Launch and isolated post-impact speed error median<=2%, p95<=5%; angular-speed error median<=5%, p95<=10%; direction median<=0.15 degrees, p95<=0.5 degrees, outside near-zero ambiguity.
requirements.verification: Track marked balls with uncertainty; use absolute low-speed bounds in TEST_PROTOCOLS.
requirements.counterexample: Infer angular velocity solely from the number patch in a blurry GIF.

requirements.title: Training and holdout separation
requirements.acceptance: Hold out >=30% of shot families, including entire speed/angle cells, before fitting. No parameter retuning on holdout; retain residuals by regime and profile.
requirements.verification: Version split manifest and evaluate untouched holdout once per candidate fit.
requirements.counterexample: Randomly split near-identical frames of one shot and call it generalization.

requirements.title: Identifiability and sensitivity
requirements.acceptance: Fit cloth/strike/ball/rail/pocket stages separately where identifiable. Report confidence/covariance, parameter sensitivity and plausible alternatives.
requirements.verification: Perturb coefficients and initial-state uncertainty; test alternative model predictions.
requirements.counterexample: One spectacular break determines all friction and restitution values.

requirements.title: Operating domain
requirements.acceptance: Published validity limits accompany each model and profile. Everyday strokes are validated; unsupported advanced shots are explicitly unavailable until their conditional requirements pass.
requirements.verification: Domain map across speed/elevation/spin/material, with boundary and beyond-boundary tests.
requirements.counterexample: Clamp unsupported elevation to another value and present it as the selected stroke.

requirements.title: Independent reproduction
requirements.acceptance: A second reviewer reproduces the key fits/plots from raw data and verifies units, source assumptions and held-out statistics before calibration signoff.
requirements.verification: Fresh analysis packet with original requirement, data, code and outputs.
requirements.counterexample: A reviewer only reads the implementer’s summary.

requirements.title: State contract
requirements.acceptance: Aiming, power/spin adjustment, committed delivery, simulation, placement and pause have explicit allowed transitions. Each transition has visual acknowledgement and a cancellation/recovery rule.
requirements.verification: Input/state transition table plus native interrupted sequences.
requirements.counterexample: Several booleans permit aim and ball placement simultaneously.

requirements.title: Tactile correspondence
requirements.acceptance: Cue pullback, selected strength, delivery velocity and result convey the same action. Soft/medium/hard strokes are distinguishable without a percentage readout and remain physically consistent with CUE.
requirements.verification: Blind 3-level strength recognition>=90% in pilot, then matched task trials.
requirements.counterexample: A different tween duration merely looks dramatic but communicates wrong strength.

requirements.title: Ready and pause
requirements.acceptance: Ready appears within one displayed frame after true settle; pause/resume introduces no time jump, late sound, stale input or moving-state freeze.
requirements.verification: Slow terminal roll, spin-only state, pause near impact/capture and long suspension.
requirements.counterexample: An arbitrary timer calls the table settled before the last ball stops.

requirements.title: Placement feedback
requirements.acceptance: Ball-in-hand has a stable translucent preview plus valid/invalid indication that is not color-only; only valid confirmation places the ball and aim begins separately.
requirements.verification: Overlapping balls, jaw edges, shelf, resize and GUI crossing with native pointer.
requirements.counterexample: An invalid red preview still accepts the click.

requirements.title: Camera continuity
requirements.acceptance: No unrequested camera motion during acquisition/delivery; optional transitions preserve aim, target visibility and picking. Motion-reduced mode removes decorative movement.
requirements.verification: Toggle/zoom/resize at each state, measure reprojection and retained shot data.
requirements.counterexample: The camera changes the apparent line while a stroke is committed.

requirements.title: Feedback honesty
requirements.acceptance: Pot, scratch, invalid stroke, miscue and rest have distinct restrained feedback tied to actual events. Cosmetic timing never changes outcomes or delays essential input.
requirements.verification: Simultaneous events, guide-off/mute and undo through the full loop.
requirements.counterexample: A celebration blocks aiming long after physical rest.

requirements.title: Original coherent direction
requirements.acceptance: Freeze a reviewed reference sheet for table construction, phenolic balls, cloth, cue, pocket lining, lighting and typography. Every asset has provenance and a declared quality/performance budget.
requirements.verification: Three matched original keyframes and one pocket/three-ball vertical slice before the full pass.
requirements.counterexample: Add high-frequency textures without resolving silhouette or lighting.

requirements.title: Ball recognition
requirements.acceptance: Color/group/number identification >=95% correct at ordinary gameplay scale in all supported views; ball versus preview identity>=95%. Include rotation/occlusion and accessible identification aid where physical markings face away.
requirements.verification: Run the prospectively frozen recognition deck in F-VISUAL with per-ball/view/experience and context/view/experience strata, explicit exposures/timeouts/misses and counts. Apply the declared descriptive sample floor and report participant-clustered uncertainty; do not claim a population lower bound of95%.
requirements.counterexample: Only enlarged stationary numbers are tested.

requirements.title: Material separation
requirements.acceptance: Cloth, cushion, wood, lining, cue and ball resin have convincing distinct scale/roughness/reflection response. Perceptual panel median>=4/5 for every material class; no crushed identities or blown white patches.
requirements.verification: Neutral/unlit/roughness views plus fixed-exposure gameplay captures and material-specific ratings.
requirements.counterexample: One attractive lighting setup conceals flat pocket geometry.

requirements.title: Temporal stability
requirements.acceptance: No visible moire, texture crawl, z-fighting, seams, shadow pop or highlight flicker in a 60 s adversarial motion deck. Numerical image-difference evidence is accompanied by real-time viewing.
requirements.verification: Slow diagonal rolls, camera motion, high-DPI/downscaled windows and side-on edges.
requirements.counterexample: A still screenshot is used to approve a shimmering weave.

requirements.title: Grounding and rotation
requirements.acceptance: Contact shadows track support/height without double blobs; spin orientation follows the simulated trajectory and remains continuous through impact, falling and undo. Render state cannot alter physical state.
requirements.verification: Marked-ball clips and world-state hashes across visual-quality toggles.
requirements.counterexample: Keep every number facing the camera by changing simulated rotation.

requirements.title: Pocket construction quality
requirements.acceptance: Visible shelf, facing, rounded lips and recessed lining have coherent depth in both cameras; no intersecting corners, floating rims, filled cutouts or detached strips. Meet GEO alignment at every LOD.
requirements.verification: Unlit topology/collision overlay and slow entry/rejection clips for all six pockets.
requirements.counterexample: Replace geometry with black circles or alter its physics radius to suit art.

requirements.title: Guide legibility
requirements.acceptance: Guide remains distinguishable without hiding contact detail; real/preview identity meets AIM gates. Overhead width 1–2 OS logical coordinate units, variation<=0.5 across DPI/zoom; lounge alternatives require an equally readable declared style.
requirements.verification: Dark/white/striped ball and cluster deck; trial recognition and pixel-width audit.
requirements.counterexample: Increase line width until it obscures the pocket acceptance margin.

requirements.title: UI readability and access
requirements.acceptance: At every supported window/DPI, essential text rendered em size>=12 OS logical coordinate units, ordinary contrast>=4.5:1 and essential non-text contrast>=3:1. Hit targets>=32 OS logical coordinate units in each dimension, primary>=40, with visible focus. Record actual design-to-OS scaling and glyph cap height; a theme-font number is not proof of rendered size.
requirements.verification: Measure actual post-scaling bounds/contrast; resize to 1100 x 700 including letterboxing; keyboard and color-vision checks.
requirements.counterexample: Design-unit font size passes while final rendered text is 8 points.

requirements.title: Table dominance
requirements.acceptance: At normal play the complete playable area, cue ball and intended target remain visible; no panel, tooltip or decorative object masks a needed line. UI density is evaluated at minimum size.
requirements.verification: Reference-task occlusion audit in both cameras and every input state.
requirements.counterexample: A permanent tutorial sidebar hides useful table area or overlaps a rail.

requirements.title: Geometry-independent appearance options
requirements.acceptance: Exposure, colorblind aids, guide style, shadow quality and motion settings preserve identical physical trajectories/events and retain required readability.
requirements.verification: State-hash replay with visual options toggled and capture comparisons.
requirements.counterexample: A material/LOD toggle changes collision geometry or ball radius.

requirements.title: Actual listening evidence
requirements.acceptance: Obtain and listen to identified gameplay audio and the local candidate; separate real game effects from trailer music/voiceover. Silent GIFs and waveform plots cannot pass sound-naturalness review.
requirements.verification: Matched playback on built-in speakers and wired headphones with written event-specific notes.
requirements.counterexample: Call reference sound natural without hearing any reference sound.

requirements.title: Contact vocabulary
requirements.acceptance: Cue, ball, cushion/facing and pocket lining/drop are recognizably distinct; each material/dynamic class has panel median>=4/5. At least 4 natural ball-impact variants and 3 variants PER other physical-contact class, unless reviewed synthesis provides equivalent natural variation. Error/miscue cues must also be distinct.
requirements.verification: Blind material/dynamic classification and repetition/fatigue listening.
requirements.counterexample: One beep is pitch-shifted into every sound class.

requirements.title: Physical intensity
requirements.acceptance: Median perceived intensity/loudness increases with declared impact energy/impulse across 9 levels; use repeated variants and report uncertainty. At the frozen calibrated volume/noise setting, softest legal contact detection>=90% and silence false positives<=5%. Full breaks retain headroom. Spectral/attack/decay quality is evaluated separately from scalar intensity.
requirements.verification: At least 9 log-spaced intensities, waveform envelope and blinded intensity-order trials.
requirements.counterexample: A hard threshold silences the new delicate stroke.

requirements.title: Dense contacts and duplicates
requirements.acceptance: Contact identity and scheduling remain auditable under the declared voice budget. Coalesce numerical duplicates per contact identity; preserve perceptually salient cue/rail/pocket events and convincing texture during realistic breaks. Document all priority/voice drops; no global unrelated-contact deletion gate.
requirements.verification: Separate 100 contacts/100 ms event-integrity stress from actual listening to plausible breaks; record voice decisions, repeated true contacts, masks and salient event recognition.
requirements.counterexample: Delete every ball collision within 16 ms of the last unrelated collision.

requirements.title: Mix and tails
requirements.acceptance: Final mix true peak<=-1 dBTP under documented oversampled measurement, no clicks/clipped samples, and >=5 ms de-click fades when stealing active tails unless an equivalent artifact-free method is validated.
requirements.verification: Worst-case overlap plus captured output; mute/unmute and voice-budget transitions.
requirements.counterexample: Every sample is clean alone but the break clips or voice stealing clicks.

requirements.title: Synchronization
requirements.acceptance: On built-in/wired baseline output, visual-contact/audio-onset median absolute offset<=10 ms and p95<=20 ms, capture uncertainty<=5 ms; no drift>5 ms over 10 minutes. Bluetooth/other outputs have separately published budgets.
requirements.verification: Calibrated high-speed display-light/photodiode capture synchronized with acoustic mic or wired electrical path; report which path, propagation/clock uncertainty,100 repeated onsets per condition and long-run drift. Ordinary 30/60 Hz video alone cannot establish 5 ms uncertainty.
requirements.counterexample: Engine callback timestamps ignore the device buffer.

requirements.title: Spatial and cosmetic consistency
requirements.acceptance: Subtle positioning matches camera/visible event; cosmetic variation and voice choices do not alter physics randomness or replay. No double cue sound after cancel/resume.
requirements.verification: Mirrored contacts, camera transitions and identical physics replays with audio toggled.
requirements.counterexample: Left contact pans right, or sample selection consumes the simulation RNG.

requirements.title: Mute and resource lifecycle
requirements.acceptance: Mute may use an artifact-free de-click ramp<=10 ms; afterward every class, queued/tail voice is digitally silent with no later burst. Repeated rack/reset/device changes retain no stale event or unbounded resource growth.
requirements.verification: Digital silence check, actual listening and long lifecycle test.
requirements.counterexample: Turning sound off leaves an already playing pocket tail at full volume.

requirements.title: Atomic settled recovery
requirements.acceptance: Valid versioned settled snapshots restore all physical fields, identities, profile and relevant counters. Unsupported/moving/malformed states are rejected without changing the live game or replacing the last good save.
requirements.verification: Round-trip, truncated writes, rename failure, wrong versions/types and moving/spinning snapshots.
requirements.counterexample: A moving IN_PLAY save loads with simulation disabled.

requirements.title: Pending snapshot coherence
requirements.acceptance: A save during delivery/motion uses one coherent restorable checkpoint and its matching counters/profile. Cancellation and restart cannot combine pre-shot balls with post-shot scoring.
requirements.verification: Save at each delivery/contact/pot phase; restore in a fresh process.
requirements.counterexample: Undo state is saved with current stroke count.

requirements.title: Undo physical equivalence
requirements.acceptance: Undo restores the entire pre-shot physical state and semantic counters exactly on one build, including orientation, pocket lifecycle and future deterministic replay.
requirements.verification: Repeat identical shot after undo and compare all ticks/events; include scratch and simultaneous captures.
requirements.counterexample: Restore positions but retain velocity or capture-suppression state.

requirements.title: Lifecycle resource stability
requirements.acceptance: After warmup,10000 headless lifecycle cycles and a 2-hour interactive soak show no monotonically growing live object count; retained memory growth<=5% after a reproducible idle plateau. No unexplained engine/resource errors.
requirements.verification: Time-series RSS/object/resource counts, with allocator/cache behavior separated from leaks.
requirements.counterexample: An aim-test teardown warning is dismissed solely because assertions passed.

requirements.title: Interruption safety
requirements.acceptance: Focus, pause, close, crash-restart and reset around any event leave one valid checkpoint, no late impulse and no duplicate sounds/scores.
requirements.verification: Boundary-timed interruption corpus and packaged restart tests.
requirements.counterexample: A generation counter cancels physics but a tween/audio callback remains live.

requirements.title: Inventory and progress
requirements.acceptance: All 16 balls retain unique stable identity; progress and pocketed state agree after every shot/undo/restore. Scratch and off-table recovery remain usable without a menu dead end.
requirements.verification: Full clear, repeated scratches, multiple pots and save/reload cycles.
requirements.counterexample: A hidden lost ball prevents the table from ever settling.

requirements.title: Declared baseline
requirements.acceptance: Record hardware/OS, renderer, release build, actual framebuffer, OS scaling, refresh, power/thermal state and startup cache state. Required baseline: Apple M4/macOS Metal,1600 x 900 and 1920 x 1080 framebuffer at 60 Hz; supported Retina modes must be profiled separately.
requirements.verification: Manifest plus actual exported process capture; no inference from window size alone.
requirements.counterexample: A1100 x 618 texture inside a 1100 x 700 window is reported as full 700 px native UI.

requirements.title: Frame-work headroom
requirements.acceptance: For a supported refresh period T=1000/refresh_hz ms, critical-path work p95<=min(12 ms,0.72*T), p99<=T over 60s each idle/play/break after declared warmup, with 3 repeats including sustained warmth. Record stages without double-counting CPU/GPU overlap.
requirements.verification: Release frame traces and stage attribution; repeat on a thermally warm session.
requirements.counterexample: Headless average simulation throughput is presented as rendered p99.

requirements.title: Presentation cadence
requirements.acceptance: At supported nominal period T=1000/refresh_hz ms, presentation interval p95<=T+0.5 ms, p99<=1.5*T; intervals>2*T are<0.1% outside frozen loading exclusions. Timestamp U95<=0.1 ms; use exact formulas and conservative uncertainty treatment, not rounded display decimals. Higher-refresh support requires its own measured profile.
requirements.verification: OS/present timestamps; report distribution, worst hitch and exclusions.
requirements.counterexample: Fixed-FPS movie export is used as proof of real-time smoothness.

requirements.title: Overload semantics
requirements.acceptance: Event/catch-up work is bounded and measured; overload does not silently drop physical time or change a shot. Unsupported sustained load has an explicit visible/recoverable policy.
requirements.verification: Injected 50/100/500 ms stalls and stress scenes; compare equal simulation ticks.
requirements.counterexample: Clamp delta and discard elapsed time while claiming deterministic real time.

requirements.title: Resource budgets
requirements.acceptance: Freeze per-profile CPU/GPU memory, mesh/texture/audio/voice budgets after a measured vertical slice; no unexplained >5% regression per checkpoint. Lifecycle stability still applies.
requirements.verification: Before/after traces with identical corpus and reported absolute values.
requirements.counterexample: Claim optimization from a different scene, device or cache state.

requirements.title: Packaged interaction
requirements.acceptance: Exported installed artifact must complete delicate touch, straight pot, thin cut, rail response, break, scratch, undo, pause and save-resume without script/resource errors. Signature/build success alone is insufficient.
requirements.verification: Run those tasks from installed/packaged app, retain video/logs and artifact hash.
requirements.counterexample: Source tests pass but the release cannot load fonts, or an external-script probe hangs.

requirements.title: Artifact provenance
requirements.acceptance: Every reviewed build identifies source/profile/test hashes and exclusion rules. Experimental engines, raw research media and temporary reports cannot silently become gameplay dependencies.
requirements.verification: Inspect package contents and confirm active engine in the installed candidate.
requirements.counterexample: A research prototype is shipped accidentally because all resources are exported.

requirements.title: Formative pilot
requirements.acceptance: Use at least 8 people with novice/experienced representation, randomized task order and declared familiarization. Record mistakes and disagreements per axis before selecting control/art alternatives.
requirements.verification: Aim,50–1000 mm placement, draw/follow, bank, pocket edge and break tasks.
requirements.counterexample: One implementer approves their own screenshot.

requirements.title: Final panel
requirements.acceptance: Final comparative study has at least 20 independent participants, at least 10 experienced and 10 novices, repeated tasks and counterbalanced order. This is a sampling floor, not power proof; pre-register participant-level paired estimator/CI, exclusions and recruitment/precision plan.
requirements.verification: Pre-register protocol/margins, collect consented anonymous task data and paired ratings.
requirements.counterexample: Treat an 8-person exploratory preference as population-wide superiority.

requirements.title: Independent axis bar
requirements.acceptance: For clarity, precision, physical plausibility, responsiveness, visual finish and sound naturalness: median>=4/5 and >=80% ratings 4–5 in EACH axis; no unresolved reproducible severe defect. Owner accepts the concrete candidate.
requirements.verification: Anchored scale and issue review per axis; expertise strata reported separately.
requirements.counterexample: A high visual score averages away unreliable cushions.

requirements.title: Reference comparison
requirements.acceptance: Compare an identified current Miniclip build and another legitimate reference on matched tasks. Proposed noninferiority margin 0.5/5 per axis: participant-level paired 95% lower bound for candidate-minus-reference must exceed -0.5 on EVERY required axis; inconclusive evidence remains inconclusive.
requirements.verification: Legitimate continuous recordings and actual tasks; preserve version/cue stats/mode and reference access limits.
requirements.counterexample: Use edited promotional GIFs as a full comparative benchmark.

requirements.title: Predictability and learning
requirements.acceptance: For preregistered matched learning blocks B1/B2, participant-level success change has paired95% lower bound>=-5 percentage points; normalized landing-error median degradation has upper bound<=0.01, and variance-ratio B2/B1 upper bound<=1.25 for nondegenerate B1. Report strata/families; unexplained spin/rail sign mismatches independently block.
requirements.verification: Use the fixed task, success windows, familiarization, timing, retry/timeout and degenerate-variance rules in F-PERCEPTION. Compare participants as independent units; use frozen recruitment and CI methods.
requirements.counterexample: Players learn around inconsistent physics without understanding it.

requirements.title: Motion and listening signoff
requirements.acceptance: Review full-speed and slow-motion clips, built-in speakers and wired headphones, normal/minimum/Retina views. Every unresolved material/perception finding has a named disposition and evidence.
requirements.verification: Separate fresh visual and listening reviews, plus owner playtest of the actual artifact.
requirements.counterexample: A waveform, still frame or build success substitutes for experienced quality.

requirements.title: Total angular momentum
requirements.acceptance: Closed free-space ball contacts conserve orbital plus intrinsic angular momentum within1e-6 relative or1e-9 kg*m²/s absolute, using the defined noncancelling reference scale. Table/cue external torques are accounted for separately.
requirements.verification: Signed spin transfer and oblique moving-pair fixtures at several reference origins; compute sum(r cross m*v + I*omega) independently.
requirements.counterexample: Check only intrinsic spin and falsely report a transfer imbalance, or omit external table torque.
